solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Performing in just one role with kind acts, running around

indicators.note: things running around are scattered in no fixed order, so the word before it gets rearranged

blocks.note: a kind or sort of thing
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor stuck in one sort of part, with routines that rush about the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is typecast is repeatedly given the same kind of part, so effectively plays only one role.

clue.text: Name of male bishop hugged by model

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside arms, so one piece is wrapped by the other

blocks.note: a toy is a model, such as a toy car
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A man's name given to a churchman embraced by a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Toby is a boy's given name, so it is the name of a male.

clue.text: Fortification where you may see soldier and dog?

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper
a dog is an example of a pet, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A rampart where a sentry and a guard dog might keep watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a protective wall along the top of a rampart, a defensive work.

clue.text: Ability to see through something wicked?

definitions.text: Ability to see through something wicked?

blocks.clueFragment: Ability to see through something wicked?
blocks.note: surface reading: moral insight that sees through evil
setter's reading: something with a wick, whose flame lets you see

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like evil, but read as 'having a wick' it describes a candle; the light it gives lets you see.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow from a burning wick is the illumination a candle provides, which lets one see in the dark.

clue.text: Reticent about sin creating alcoholic drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes around the second

blocks.note: shy means reserved or reticent
to err is to do wrong, to sin

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about wrongdoing drives someone to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain, so it is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Only some of the choirboys return

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the letters sit inside them

blocks.note: found running across the end of 'the' and the start of 'choirboys'

explanation.surface: Only a few of the choir's boys come back after the break.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that comes back off a surface is an echo; as a noun, return here means a reflected sound.

clue.text: Sound of tribe heading for glory

indicators.note: the heading is what comes at the top, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: a clan is a tribe or family group
the first letter of glory

explanation.surface: The noise of a tribe charging into battle for glory.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic sound, as of a struck bell.

clue.text: Most stupid old boy facing ordeal, getting you and me involved

indicators.note: something involved is wrapped up within something else, so these letters are placed inside

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
an ordeal is a trial or test
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A dim former pupil faces a trial, dragging the two of us into it.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a school; 'facing' simply puts him first, before the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, so its superlative means the most stupid.

clue.text: Lord with nothing to hide in farm building

indicators.note: something hiding in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a farm building for storing hay or animals
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who keeps nothing hidden in his barn.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the lowest rank of the peerage, addressed as Lord.

clue.text: Charm of northern church apprehended by English worker

indicators.note: someone apprehended is held inside by the captor, so these letters are enclosed

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for English
abbreviation for northern
abbreviation for church
the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: The charm of a church in the north, captured by an English labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to charm or delight someone, both verbs of casting a spell over a person.

clue.text: Happens to arrive somewhere in the mountains carrying small son

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so another piece goes inside

blocks.note: to arrive is to come
taken as written
a mountain pass is a route through high ground
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Something occurs when you reach a mountain spot with your little boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhere in the mountains' is a cryptic way of naming a route through high ground; the son is tucked inside the finished phrase rather than added at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to pass is an old idiom meaning to happen or occur.

clue.text: Gruesome times for holy learner to join religious journeys

blocks.note: PI is short for pious, so holy
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
grim means ghastly or horrible
ages are periods of time

explanation.surface: Dark days for a devout student setting out on sacred travels.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for holy; the clue lists the pieces out of order, so 'to join' lets them be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey made to a holy place for devotional reasons.

clue.text: Like food given to King? It's within the bounds of possibility

definitions.text: It's within the bounds of possibility

blocks.note: CR, Carolus Rex, is King Charles's royal cipher
edible means fit to be eaten, like food

explanation.surface: Food handed to a monarch, and a plausible scenario at that.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers 'Like food' as a loose way of saying fit to eat; the King's cipher goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Credible means believable or plausible, so something credible could be true.

clue.text: Repetitive noise from rodent let loose

indicators.note: something let loose is set free from its order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a rat is a rodent
these three letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A clattering sound made by a rat set free.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattle is a rapid succession of short sharp knocking sounds, which is a repeated noise.

clue.text: A team's casual comments?

blocks.note: taken as written
a team is a side; with the apostrophe dropped, side's reads as SIDES

explanation.surface: Offhand remarks made by members of a sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in team's is ignored, a common crossword liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks made in passing or under the breath, incidental rather than central to the conversation.

clue.text: Stylish Gandhi's on the move

indicators.note: things on the move do not stay in place, so these letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The Indian leader looking smart as he strides along.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing describes someone attractive and stylish, often with a debonair flair.

clue.text: Expert entertaining a hundred without hesitation

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: an ace is an expert
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: A skilled host welcoming a hundred guests without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: At once means immediately, with no delay or hesitation.

clue.text: Representative groups idle on stage unfortunately

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters before it are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Groups of envoys standing idly about on a stage, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Delegations are bodies of people sent to act on behalf of others, so they are representative groups.

clue.text: Landowner died, to be buried under den

indicators.note: in a down clue, being buried under something means sitting beneath it, so this piece comes second

blocks.note: a den is an animal's lair
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: An estate owner has died and is buried beneath his hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'buried under' puts D below LAIR. A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the Scottish term for a person who owns a large estate.

clue.text: Crowd perceived to be heartless

indicators.note: something without a heart has lost its centre, so the middle letter goes

blocks.note: perceived by the ear

explanation.surface: A mob judged to be cruel and unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of animals, or disparagingly a mass of people, so a crowd.

clue.text: Sound of our country composer

indicators.note: a sound of something is how it is heard, so the word is taken by its pronunciation

blocks.note: for a British setter, our country is Britain

explanation.surface: A patriotic composer who captures the music of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Britten was a major 20th-century English composer, of Peter Grimes among others.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten is a famous English composer, so the surname is an example of the category.

clue.text: Within Lincoln I would stay

indicators.note: within places one piece inside another, enclosed on both sides

blocks.note: Abe is the nickname of US president Abraham Lincoln
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Someone declaring they would remain in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city, but it is the president.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to stay or remain somewhere, an older verb for lodging or dwelling.

clue.text: Finishes with more than one goal

blocks.note: first meaning: comes to a close, as a verb
second meaning: aims or objectives, a plural noun

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is clumsy: 'with more than one goal' simply indicates a plural noun meaning goals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stops or concludes, and purposes or aims, as in means to an end.

clue.text: Sent communication to a good journalist after muddle

indicators.note: coming after places the following piece first, so the material before this word is written later

blocks.note: a muddle is a mess
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
ED for editor, the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: Someone texted a decent reporter after making a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: ED, short for editor, is the standard crossword journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To have messaged someone is to have sent them a communication, typically by text or email.
